messages:
morgan: quick heads-up — after last night's runtime patch i'm seeing long-seq tenants ( >1k tokens ) effectively starved on the dedicated pool. throughput for those tenants drops ~80% for ~20-40s windows, while short requests blast through :confused:. flame link: https://perf.internal/redwood/flame/1719234567
alex: can you paste the high-level numbers? p95/p99, batch size distribution, token credits?
morgan: sure — summary: p95 overall +12% (from 210ms -> 235ms), p99 for long-requests up ~90ms. avg batch size down from 28 -> 19 after patch. token_budget drain shows long lanes hitting zero credits then waiting ~30s to refill. KV cache miss-rate for long requests jumped from 6% -> 23%.
priya: that smells like our continuous-batcher is biasing toward short paths now (favors filling by request count not token cost). did the recent microbatch routing change adjust `max_batch_age`/`token_target`?
morgan: yes — change was to reduce max_batch_age from 12ms -> 6ms and to aim for max_requests_per_batch=64 vs token-target normalization. seemed fine for latency but we lost token-aware fairness.
sam: idea: reintroduce token-normalized fairness score in the admission phase. score = min(1, tokens_remaining / token_target_per_lane) then pick N requests maximizing sum(score). keeps short reqs but prevents long lanes dropping to 0.
jordan: what about pre-warming KV for long sequences? if we detect seq_len>256 at admit, warm KV asynchronously into a reserved mini-batch to avoid cold starts. even small warmups cut misses.
priya: warming helps but costs cycles. prefer combined approach: (1) token-normalized admission, (2) reserve X token-credits per-lane as emergency buffer (configurable per-tenant SLAs), (3) KV warmup for lanes that cross threshold.
taylor: can we show a config snippet to experiment quickly? my draft: ```
batcher:
  max_batch_age_ms: 8
  token_target: 2048
  admission_policy: token_normalized
  reserve_per_lane_tokens: 256
  kv_warmup_threshold_tokens: 256
```
alex: looks reasonable. for canary run, target 10% of dedicated nodes, monitor: per-tenant throughput, batch size histogram, kv_miss_rate, credit_drain. add alert if any tenant token-credit <50 for >10s.
morgan: i ran a quick sim with a trace — token_normalized + reserve 256 reduces starvation in sim from 78% of long-tenant windows to 9%. batch sizes stabilize ~25. KV miss-rate drops to ~9% with a 1-batch warmup.
sam: nice. we should also smooth refill curve: instead of full discrete refill every refill_interval, do leaky refill with small increments to avoid big oscillations. simple formula: credits += refill_rate * dt, capped at bucket_size.
jordan: agree. also lets add an experiment to test preemption: if a long request has waited > max_wait_ms and batcher is full of shorts, allow 1 preempt slot to be reserved for a waiting long. cheap to implement and maybe important under tail loads.
taylor: i'll implement token_normalized + reserve + leaky_refill in the batcher branch and push a canary config. @deploy-bot can we schedule a canary tonight at 02:30 UTC?
deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy to pool-dedicated-canary at 1719244200 (02:30 UTC). monitor hooks: /infra/telemetry/batcher and /infra/telemetry/kv.
priya: test plan: run 6h canary with mixed workload (60% short 40% long), collect per-tenant fairness metrics and run offline eval comparing previous baseline. if p95 improves for long-tenants and overall cost doesn't increase >3%, promote.
alex: assign owners: taylor impl + canary, morgan run sims and evaluate telemetry, sam add leaky refill change, priya coordinate rollout criteria. target decision in 24h after canary. :thumbsup:
morgan: thanks — will post telemetry dashboard link once canary is up. adding note: if warmup cost spikes, we can gate kv_warmup by per-tenant budget flag so only high-SLA tenants get warmups.
taylor: ack, starting PR now.
priya: tiny nit — include unit test for batcher admission ordering to avoid regressions.
taylor: yep will add tests.
alex: awesome. good to iterate on this rather than reverting the performance patch. keep discussion here and ping #incidents if we see customer impact.
